title: Practice Test Traps
description: Look-alikes a full practice test caught: the four Guardrails filters, fixes for overfitting and for imbalanced data, anomaly detection without labels, explanation methods, embeddings, and a few services. Most cards are learned here and listed on their topic's own deck too. A few pairs from the foundation-models deck (Top K and Top P, fine-tuning and continued pre-training) are copied in so they're set against each other; those copies keep their own progress.

cards.definition: Bedrock Guardrails filter that detects harmful text or images in prompts and responses by predefined categories (hate, insults, sexual, violence, misconduct, prompt attack), each with a strength you set
Bedrock Guardrails filter that blocks subjects you describe in plain language, such as investment advice in a banking assistant, by meaning rather than by keyword
Bedrock Guardrails filter that blocks exact custom words or phrases, such as competitor names, plus a ready-made profanity list
Bedrock Guardrails filter that detects PII, or custom patterns you define with regex, in prompts and responses and blocks or masks it, with no retraining of the model
Unsupervised neural network that compresses its input and rebuilds it; trained only on normal data, it rebuilds unusual data poorly, so a high reconstruction error flags an anomaly
SageMaker AI built-in unsupervised algorithm that gives each data point an anomaly score; high scores mark anomalies such as unexpected spikes in time series data
Penalty during training, such as L1 (Lasso) or L2 (Ridge), that discourages an overly complex model; reduces overfitting but does not fix biased or imbalanced data
Regularization for neural networks that randomly switches off some neurons during training, so the network can't lean on memorized paths; reduces overfitting
Ending training once results on validation data stop improving, before the model starts learning noise; reduces overfitting

Trying different settings chosen before training, such as learning rate, regularization strength, dropout rate, and epochs, to find the version that performs best on validation data; can reduce overfitting without new data

Creating new training examples from existing data, by small changes such as flips and rotations or by generating synthetic examples; adds examples for underrepresented groups to reduce bias, and reduces overfitting
Fine-tuning a pretrained model on plain domain-specific text, with no prompt-response pairs, so it learns industry jargon and terminology; changes the model's weights (SageMaker JumpStart)

Training a new model from an existing model's artifacts plus an expanded dataset, instead of from scratch, to save time; used when predictions have slipped because new data has patterns the old model never saw
Feature attribution from game theory that gives each feature an importance value for one particular prediction: a local explanation (used by SageMaker Clarify)
Chart of the marginal effect a feature has on the model's predicted outcome across the dataset: a global explanation (produced by SageMaker Clarify)
Word embedding algorithm that gives each word one vector, so it can't tell apart the meanings of the same word in different sentences
Transformer-based language model that reads the words on both sides, so the same word gets different embeddings in different contexts, like play the noun and play the verb
One development environment that brings AWS data, analytics, ML, and generative AI tools together, where teams build and share work in governed projects
Amazon Bedrock playground for building and sharing no-code generative AI mini-apps; for learning and experimenting, not governed enterprise work

SageMaker catalog of model versions, with their metadata such as training metrics and an approval status; used to deploy approved versions, including through CI/CD pipelines, but it doesn't train models
Generated records that keep the statistical patterns of real data without containing real people; used to train when real data is sensitive or scarce

Hiding direct identifiers before training: masking hides the values, and data tokenization swaps them for surrogate tokens that only a protected lookup table can reverse. Encryption alone doesn't do this, since the training job decrypts the data
Inference parameter that sets the number of most-likely candidates the model considers for the next token: a fixed-size pool, such as the 50 likeliest
Inference parameter that sets the percentage of most-likely candidates the model considers for the next token: the top P% of the cumulative probability, so the pool size varies
Further training a pretrained model on a smaller, task-specific labeled dataset
Training a model on additional domain-specific unlabeled data
Fine-tuning on instruction and response pairs so the model follows user directions
